newsitem.title: RUSSIA: INTERVIEW-Volga-Dnepr sees more big cargoes in 97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Volga-Dnepr sees more big cargoes in 97.

text.p: A senior official of the Volga-Dnepr commercial airline said on Tuesday that Russian cargo airlines would boost their use of Antonov 124 planes and that heavy cargoes worth a total of $170 million were moved last year.
"The number of such transportations will increase greatly this year," Volga-Dnepr commercial director Grigory Stilbans told Reuters.
The planes each have a capacity of up to 120 tonnes.

Stilbans said a joint venture with the Ulyanovsk company and Britain's HeavyLift company made up 64 percent cent of world sales in super-heavy cargoes, while a joint venture between Ukraine's Antonov and Britain's Air Foyle made up a further 23 percent.
Russian firms Ayaks and Russian Trans Charter shared another 3-4 percent of the market.

Volga-Dnepr which bought a seventh An-124 Ruslan aircraft last year, used the freighters for $101.4 million of the company's total 1996 sales of $111 million. "Our Ruslans carried 36 percent more cargo last year than in 1995," Stilbans said.
Volga-Dnepr also operates three Ilyushin-76, one An-12 and one An-32. It carried 45,100 tonnes of cargo last year, compared with 39,633 tonnes of cargo in 1995.
"We have enough planes for market demand and do not plan to buy more aircraft this year," Stilbans said.

Stilbans said over 10 percent of 1996 sales, or $11.7 million, were between the company's Ulyanovsk base and China. But cargo routes to India and Thailand were less profitable last year as orders eased.
"We do not expect a sharp increase in sales volume in transportation of general cargoes in 1997 because this segment of the market is very competitive," he said.
